interviewQuestions.question: Compare direct-mapped, set-associative, and fully associative caches. Why do real CPUs use set-associative?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
⭐ **Q: Compare direct-mapped, set-associative, and fully associative caches. Why do real CPUs use set-associative?**

Direct-mapped: each block gets one slot — cheapest hardware, prone to conflict misses. Fully associative: a block goes anywhere — zero conflicts, but a comparator per slot, unscalable past small structures like TLBs.

Set-associative sits between: an address picks one set, within it any of N ways. Only N comparators per set, avoiding most conflicts — why virtually every L1/L2/L3 is 4-, 8-, or 16-way.

**Testing:** whether you explain *why* the middle ground wins, not just recite three names.
